_note: Easy and moderate walks only: under 5 miles round trip, no sustained steep grades. 'kid' is our own 1-5 for ages 1-7 plus grandparents; 'g' is the Google rating where one exists.

trails.name: Cataract Falls
trails.why: The shortest walk to a waterfall in the park, starting behind the visitor center. Flat enough for a two-year-old on foot. Reviewers are unanimous that strollers die on the roots, so Snejana rides. One review saw a bear in the lot; look before you unbuckle.

trails.name: Sugarlands Valley Nature Trail
trails.area: Newfound Gap Rd, 0.3 mi past the visitor center
trails.stroller: Yes, the only fully paved trail
trails.why: A paved loop along the West Prong with an old chimney and the river the whole way. Built for wheelchairs, so it works for a stroller and for anyone's knees. The one trail where all five of you move at the same speed.

trails.name: Gatlinburg Trail
trails.area: Sugarlands to the edge of town
trails.rt: Up to 3.8 mi, turn around anywhere
trails.why: An old road along the Little Pigeon, flat, wide, and one of two trails in the park that take dogs. Walk twenty minutes out and back and you've had a hike; walk the whole thing and you're at the Gatlinburg Bypass. Good on a damp day because gravel doesn't turn to mud.
trails.day: Any morning, or Plan B for Wednesday and Friday
trails.photo: Little River Road - October 2025 - Sarah Stierch.jpg

trails.name: Elkmont Nature Trail
trails.why: A quiet creekside loop with interpretive signs and bridges the kids will want to stand on. Reviewers call it good for young children and the elderly in the same breath. The old Elkmont cabins at the trailhead are an extra ten minutes of poking around.
trails.day: Wednesday afternoon if the Cove was short, or Plan B

trails.name: Little River Trail from Elkmont
trails.rt: Up to 4.6 mi to Huskey Branch Falls
trails.time: 2 to 3 hours full, or 45 min out and back
trails.why: The old logging railbed, so the grade never steepens. Follows the Little River the entire way with pools and boulders to look at. Turn around at any point; the small cascade at Huskey Branch is 2.3 miles in and is the reward if the kids have it in them. Grandparent-friendly footing.
trails.photo: Little River Road - October 2025 - Sarah Stierch.jpg

trails.name: Metcalf Bottoms to Little Greenbrier School
trails.surface: Dirt, roots, a few short hills
trails.why: From the picnic tables by the river to a one-room 1882 schoolhouse with a cemetery. Short rolling hills, lots of roots, nothing steep. The picnic area itself, with the shallow river, is worth the stop even if nobody walks. The Walker Sisters cabin adds another 1.1 miles each way; skip it with the little two.
trails.day: Wednesday on the way back from Cades Cove
trails.photo: Little River Road - October 2025 - Sarah Stierch.jpg

trails.name: Middle Prong Trail to Lynn Camp Prong Cascades
trails.rt: 1.4 mi to the cascades, up to 4.6 mi
trails.why: The best waterfall-per-effort ratio in the park: a wide old road climbs gently beside the river and the long Lynn Camp Prong cascades start at 0.6 miles. A 1930s Cadillac rusting in the woods sits at 2.3 miles if Cash wants a goal. The last three miles of road to the trailhead are gravel.
trails.day: Pairs with Cades Cove, it's on the way, or its own morning

trails.name: Cove Hardwood Nature Trail
trails.area: Chimneys Picnic Area, Newfound Gap Rd
trails.why: Old-growth trees as big as anything in the park on a short loop that climbs a hill and comes back down. Reviewers say fine for little hikers; the grade is short but real, so grandparents take it slow. The 50-cent trail guide at the start is worth it. Picnic tables and restrooms at the car.
trails.day: Friday on the way down from Kuwohi
trails.photo: Chimney Tops viewed from Chimney Tops overlook, May 2017.jpg

trails.name: Noah Ogle Place
trails.area: Cherokee Orchard Rd, 3 mi from downtown
trails.rt: 0.75 mi loop, or 200 ft to the cabin
trails.surface: Rocky, wet, uneven on the far side
trails.why: The cabin, barn and tub mill are a hundred yards from the road and good for all three kids. The nature-trail loop beyond is loose wet rock and reviewers found it slippery and harder than it looks; do the cabin, skip the loop with the little two.
trails.photo: Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail - March 2024 - Sarah Stierch 03.jpg

trails.name: Porters Creek Trail, first mile
trails.area: Greenbrier, 6 mi east of town on US-321
trails.rt: 2 mi to the farm site, 3.8 mi to Fern Branch Falls
trails.gain: 200 ft to the farm site, 650 ft to the falls
trails.surface: Old gravel road, then dirt and footlogs
trails.why: The first mile is a gravel road along a loud creek to an old cemetery and farm site with a cantilever barn. That's the kid version and it's a good one. The falls beyond are moderate with a real climb and narrow footlog bridges; not for this crew, fine for Cash and one adult another year.

trails.name: Kuwohi tower
trails.stroller: Technically yes, but you'll regret it
trails.why: The one steep walk on this list, kept because the view is the best in the park and the road closes for the winter the day after you leave. Benches every hundred yards. Grandparents go slow and stop at each one. It is 15 to 20 degrees colder up here than the cabin.
trails.photo: Observation Tower in Fog, Clingmans Dome (Kuwahi), Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Swain County, NC.jpg

trails.name: Oconaluftee River Trail
trails.why: Only if you decide to drive over Newfound Gap into North Carolina: flat river path from the visitor center, benches, and the elk herd that grazes the field by the Mountain Farm Museum most mornings. The farm museum is free and has animals. Not this trip's plan, but the best elk sighting in the park and a stroller trail.
trails.day: Only if you go over the gap

trails.name: Pigeon Forge Riverwalk, Patriot Park to The Island
trails.why: Not a park trail, but the most useful flat walk in Pigeon Forge: paved along the river from the Old Mill to The Island, lit for Winterfest after dark. Park free at Patriot Park, walk one way, trolley back.
trails.dest: Patriot Park, 236 Old Mill Ave, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863

not_this_trip: 2.6 mi, 500 ft of climb, slick near the falls. Cash and one adult, another year.
5 mi with three climbs and a dangerous pool at the bottom. No.
Steep and long. Not with anyone under seven.
From Kuwohi, 3.6 mi with a 600 ft climb back out at 6,000 ft. Not with the baby in November.
Both closed or rebuilt sections and both too steep for this crew.
